newsitem.title: CHINA: China bans using deposit receipts as gifts.
newsitem.headline: China bans using deposit receipts as gifts.

text.p: The People's Bank of China, the central bank, has banned commercial banks and postal savings offices from issuing transferable receipts for deposits in the form of gift cards, the Financial News said on Wednesday.
"These could trigger unfair competition and unhealthy tendencies," said a brief circular published in the newspaper.
It gave no further details and central bank officials declined comment.
But officials at state-run commercial banks said the gift cards may have been used by customers to make illegal payments.
Under the scheme, customers could deposit money in a bank account and give the funds to someone else as a gift. The gift cards do not carry the name of the depositor and can be transferred easily.
"We discontinued the service one month ago," said an official at the Beijing branch of a state bank.
"The service was suspended because it was believed to be playing a role in official corruption," he said.
